blocks.text: A pure water sachet, a plastic bucket, a raincoat and a bottle crate all began life as one small gas molecule: ethene. Everything that makes ethene so useful comes from a single feature of its structure, the carbon-to-carbon double bond.

blocks.title: Unsaturated hydrocarbons
blocks.text: Alkenes contain at least one carbon-to-carbon double bond and have the general formula CnH2n. Alkynes contain a carbon-to-carbon triple bond and have the general formula CnH2n-2. Both are described as unsaturated because they can add extra atoms across the multiple bond.

blocks.caption: Comparing the three hydrocarbon series. Note that there is no member of the alkene or alkyne series with only one carbon

blocks.markdown:
## Why unsaturation means reactivity

A double bond consists of one strong sigma bond and one weaker pi bond. The pi bond has exposed electron density above and below the line joining the two carbons, which attracts electron-seeking species. The pi bond breaks readily while the sigma bond survives, and the two carbons pick up one new atom each.

That is an **addition reaction**, and it is the defining behaviour of alkenes and alkynes.

items: Hydrogenation: C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6, using a nickel catalyst at about 150 degrees Celsius. This is how liquid vegetable oil is hardened into margarine
Halogenation: C2H4 + Br2 -> C2H4Br2, which happens at room temperature and decolourises bromine water
Hydration: C2H4 + H2O -> C2H5OH, with steam and phosphoric acid catalyst, the industrial route to ethanol
Hydrogen halide addition: C2H4 + HCl -> C2H5Cl
Polymerisation: many ethene molecules join to form poly(ethene), the plastic in sachets and buckets

blocks.title: Distinguishing an alkene from an alkane
blocks.prompt: You are given two unlabelled colourless gases, one ethane and one ethene. Describe a simple laboratory test that identifies each, stating the observation and the reason.

steps.text: Choose the reagent: bromine water, which is orange or reddish-brown.
Bubble a sample of each gas separately through a few cm3 of bromine water in a test tube and shake.
The tube containing ethene is decolourised rapidly: the orange colour disappears, leaving a colourless solution.
This is because bromine adds across the double bond: C2H4 + Br2 -> C2H4Br2, 1,2-dibromoethane, which is colourless. The coloured bromine is consumed.
The tube containing ethane stays orange, because ethane is saturated and can only react with bromine by substitution, which needs ultraviolet light and does not occur in the dark.
Conclusion: the gas that decolourises bromine water in the dark is the alkene.

blocks.answer: Bubble each gas through bromine water; ethene decolourises it immediately while ethane leaves it orange

blocks.markdown:
## Polymerisation

In **addition polymerisation**, many identical unsaturated monomers join end to end with no other product formed. The double bond opens and the units link into a long chain.

n CH2=CH2 -> (-CH2-CH2-)n

| Monomer | Polymer | Everyday use in Nigeria |
|---|---|---|
| Ethene | Poly(ethene) | Water sachets, buckets, plastic bags |
| Propene | Poly(propene) | Bottle crates, ropes, chairs |
| Chloroethene | Poly(chloroethene), PVC | Electrical cable insulation, pipes |
| Tetrafluoroethene | PTFE | Non-stick pan coatings |

These polymers are non-biodegradable, which is why discarded sachets block drains and worsen flooding in Lagos and Port Harcourt.

### Ethyne

Ethyne, C2H2, is prepared in the laboratory by adding water to calcium carbide:

CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2

It burns in oxygen with a very hot flame, which is why the oxy-acetylene torch is used for welding and cutting steel. Ethyne also decolourises bromine water, and because it has a triple bond it can add two molecules of bromine per molecule.

blocks.title: State the conditions
blocks.text: Marks in organic chemistry depend heavily on conditions. Write 'nickel catalyst, 150 degrees Celsius' for hydrogenation and 'steam, phosphoric acid catalyst' for hydration. An equation without conditions rarely earns full credit.

points: Alkenes are CnH2n with a double bond; alkynes are CnH2n-2 with a triple bond.
Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo addition reactions because the pi bond breaks readily.
Bromine water is decolourised by alkenes and alkynes but not by alkanes in the dark.
Hydrogenation with a nickel catalyst converts vegetable oils into margarine.
Addition polymerisation of ethene and propene produces the plastics used in sachets, bags and crates.
Ethyne is made from calcium carbide and water and burns with a very hot flame used in welding.
